summary: @ornikar/jest-config preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: The package's `preinstall` hook runs `setup.mjs`, an obfuscator.io-style script with hex-suffixed identifiers and wrapper lookup objects hiding `fs.createWriteStream` and `execFileSync` calls. If `bun` is not on PATH, setup.mjs downloads a pinned Bun release from github.com/oven-sh/bun, extracts and chmods it executable in a temp directory, and invokes it against the sibling file `math_init.js` — a 727KB single-line script using rotating string-array obfuscation (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header, `WV8StW` rotator function, hex-prefixed variables). The advertised functionality of the package is a Jest preset (`jest-preset.js`), which has no legitimate need to fetch an alternate JavaScript runtime or execute a half-megabyte opaque blob at install time. The alternate-runtime dispatch (Bun rather than Node) is consistent with evading Node-based install-time scanners. Installing this version causes arbitrary attacker-controlled code, whose behavior cannot be determined without execution, to run on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
